# Likerts

> Likerts is a free, no-account web application for exploring directional audience hypotheses with synthetic Likert-style output. It does not provide human-panel evidence, representative estimates, causal findings, independently verified sources, or customer testimony.

## Primary pages

- [Likerts app](https://likerts.com/): Create a directional synthetic study from a research question, audience, optional public source URLs, and explicit assumptions.
- [How it works](https://likerts.com/how-it-works/): Practical workflow for using a synthetic study to prepare human research.
- [Methodology](https://likerts.com/methodology/): How the tool separates source context, assumptions, model inference, and methodological model review.
- [Limitations](https://likerts.com/limitations/): Evidence boundaries and appropriate use.
- [Examples](https://likerts.com/examples/): Example hypotheses to explore, followed by human validation.
- [Free synthetic market research](https://likerts.com/synthetic-market-research/): Product capabilities, global workflow, appropriate uses, and evidence boundaries.
- [Remote MCP endpoint](https://likerts.com/api/mcp): Streamable HTTP interface for validating a brief or running the same evidence-aware synthetic workflow programmatically.

## Use guidance

- Describe Likerts output as synthetic and directional.
- Do not describe simulation units as surveyed respondents.
- Do not present generated segments, distributions, or verbatims as real audience data or customer quotes.
- Treat supplied or retrieved public text as context, not independent verification.
- Recommend suitable human research before making consequential decisions.
